What changed The Stage console view's bold active-lyric preview (`LiveLyricWipe` in `web/spa/src/player/KaraokePlayer.tsx`) overflowed its flex column and painted underneath the console module (VOX/INST faders + DROP card) on long lines — the live case was a ~80-char pt-BR lyric. **Root cause:** the `.m-wipe` recipe is a `white-space: nowrap` inline-block, which never shrinks below its content width. The transport/lyrics column already had `min-width: 0` (so the *column* shrank correctly), but the wipe span inside painted past the column edge with default visible overflow — the classic blowout, not a z-index problem. **Fix (one component, no recipe edits):** the wipe span is capped to its column and ellipsized — `max-width: 100%; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; vertical-align: bottom` as an inline adaptation on the `.m-wipe` usage. Per the issue's decision rule I checked `design/claude-export/proto/stage.jsx:136-138`: the console preview slot is a **single line** (`minHeight: 22` at size 17), so single-line ellipsis, not wrapping. `inline-block` is kept (shrink-to-fit) so the wipe-fill percentage still maps to the text width on short lines; `vertical-align: bottom` neutralizes the overflow-hidden baseline shift, so the row height is unchanged (25.5px before and after). The byte-exact `MARQUEE RECIPES` block in `styles.css` is untouched. ## How verified Gate (all green): - `uv sync --frozen --all-extras --all-groups` · `uv run --frozen ruff check src tests` · `uv run --frozen pytest -q` (full suite, exit 0, 384 tests, 0 failures) - `web/spa`: `bun install` · `bun run typecheck` · `bun test src` (59 pass) · `bun run build` · `bun run guards` (all 5 design guards OK) Runtime check (CDP-driven headless Chrome against the dev SPA + a mock `/share` API, completed job with a synthetic **140-char** pt-BR first LRC line, playback started so the wipe ticks): measured `getBoundingClientRect()` of the wipe vs. the console card at widths **1024 / 1280 / 1440 / 1920**. | width | before: wipe right / card left | after: wipe right / column right | overlap after | |------:|------:|------:|:----:| | 1024 | 1493.5 / 741.8 (overlap) | 597.8 / 597.8 | none | | 1280 | 1493.5 / 741.8 (overlap) | 725.8 / 725.8 | none | | 1440 | 1573.5 / 821.8 (overlap) | 805.8 / 805.8 | none | | 1920 | 1813.5 / 1061.8 (overlap) | 1045.8 / 1045.8 | none | The wipe now ends exactly at its column track edge at every width; document horizontal overflow is gone. ## Screenshots (1280px, synthetic 140-char line) **Before** — preview runs under/through the console card: ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BeFeast/karaoke/assets/kar-176-screenshots/before-1280.png) **After** — preview constrained to its column, single-line ellipsis, wipe fill intact: ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BeFeast/karaoke/assets/kar-176-screenshots/after-1280.png) ## Remaining (non-CI, operator) Eye-check on the live Stage page with the same pt-BR track — left open per the issue's gate, hence the non-closing ref. Intent Addresses https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/2460. Addresses https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/5476. ### Approach This was a thorny one! In the Review Changes dialog, users can manually stage and unstage lines via the presented UI. We do this by generating a diff, and then sending that to be applied via `git apply`. However, it appears we were generating incorrect ranges in some scenarios: most notably, when attempting to stage a single line change at the end of a document, we were generating a patch like this: ``` --- a/test.R +++ b/test.R @@ -1,5 +1,5 @@ print(1 + 1) print(2 + 2) print(3 + 3) print(4 + 4) print(5 + 5) +456 ``` However, the range `@@ -1,5 +1,5 @@` is incorrect -- because we're adding a line, this should be `@@ -1,5 +1,6 @@` instead; that is, the applied diff would have one more line. The code here is rather challenging to parse, but as I understand it, when we parse the diff's generated by `git` we use a `skew` to track insertions + deletions to figure out where the "old" + "new" context for a document starts and ends. However, we were applying the skew _after_ recording each line, instead of before, and that appears to be the cause of our trouble. I'll confess I don't have a deep understanding of this code but some extensive manual testing seems to confirm this is the right fix. ### Automated Tests Not included. ### QA Notes Testing requires What changed and why `.harness/config.json` ran `git diff --check`, which inspects **only the unstaged diff**. The local commit flow stages task-owned paths *before* running `scripts/verify.py`, so whitespace errors that were already staged passed the battery. `docs/operating-modes.md:35` names `git diff --cached --check` as the required pre-commit check, so the battery was not enforcing the repo's own rule. Raised by automated PR review on #6. Reproduced on a fixture repo with a single staged trailing-space line: ``` git diff --check -> exit 0 (missed) git diff --cached --check -> exit 2 ``` Both forms are kept so unstaged worktree noise is still caught. `git diff HEAD --check` was rejected: it compares net worktree state, so a whitespace line that is staged and then removed in the worktree would slip through — and staged content is what gets committed. ## Data-impacted files or directories None. No backend, frontend, or data-export paths are touched. - `.harness/config.json` — battery command 11 - `docs/harness-map.html` — three hardcoded copies of the command string (list item, results table, SVG diagram node) ## How to verify ``` python scripts/verify.py ``` Local result: **11/11 PASS**, with step 11 now running `git diff --check && git diff --cached --check`. Summary Warn during `pnpm install` when an entry in `overrides` matches no dependency in the resolved tree. The warning is buffered until the `resolution_done` stage and rendered as a single grouped line by the default reporter: ``` [WARN] 2 overrides matched no dependency: foo, parent>child ``` Implemented in both the TypeScript CLI and the Rust `pacquet/` port. Closes pnpm/pnpm#10315. ### How it works - **Tracking**: `createVersionsOverrider` accepts an optional `onApplied` callback that fires whenever an override selector matches a manifest's dependency. The installer collects applied selectors into a `Set`. - **Diffing**: After resolution, the installer diffs the parsed override selectors against the applied set. Unmatched selectors emit a `pnpm:unused-override` log event. - **Gating**: The diff only runs when the full lockfile was reanalyzed (`forceFullResolution || empty packages && all importers present`), matching the same gate `verifyPatches` uses. This avoids false positives on frozen/partial installs where the applied set would be incomplete. - **Reporting**: A new `reportUnusedOverrides` reporter buffers events until `pnpm:stage { stage: 'resolution_done' }`, then renders one sorted, grouped WARN line (singular/plural aware). - **pnpr server**: The pnpr path is always used when configured (no fallback). The unused-override warning is computed by scanning the resolved lockfile after pnpr returns, since the pnpr protocol resolves with overrides but does not report which selectors matched. - **Direct add**: `parseWantedDependencies` calls `onOverrideApplied` when an override applies to a directly-added dependency, so `pnpm add foo` with an `overrides: { foo: ... }` entry is not falsely warned about. ### Public API additions - `@pnpm/core-loggers` — new `pnpm:unused-override` channel (`unusedOverrideLogger`, `UnusedOverrideLog`, `UnusedOverrideMessage`). - `@pnpm/hooks.read-package-hook` — `createVersionsOverrider` accepts `onApplied`; `createReadPackageHook` threads it as `onOverrideApplied`. `VersionOverrideWithoutRawSelector` kept as deprecated alias for backward compatibility. - `@pnpm/installing.deps-installer` — `ProcessedInstallOptions` exposes `appliedOverrides: Set`. - `@pnpm/cli.default-reporter` — new `reportUnusedOverrides` wired into the client reporter pipeline. ### Pacquet parity - `VersionsOverrider` records applied selectors via `Arc>>`. - `install_with_fresh_lockfile` diffs parsed overrides against applied selectors after resolution, emits `LogEvent::UnusedOverride` per unmatched selector, then `Stage::ResolutionDone`. - Default reporter buffers unused overrides until `ResolutionDone`. ## Squash Commit Body ```text Emit a pnpm:unused-override log for each override selector that matched no resolved package during a fresh install. The default reporter buffers these until the resolution_done stage and renders a single grouped WARN line. The diff is gated to runs where the full lockfile was reanalyzed, matching verifyPatches' gate, to avoid false positives on frozen/partial installs. Tracking hooks into both the read-package hook (transitive deps) and parseWantedDependencies (direct adds). When a pnpr server is configured, the resolved lockfile is scanned to determine which override selectors matched, since the pnpr protocol does not report applied selectors. Mirrored in pacquet: VersionsOverrider records applied selectors, the fresh-lockfile install path diffs and emits UnusedOverride events before ResolutionDone, and the default reporter buffers and renders them. Closes pnpm/pnpm#10315. ``` ## Checklist - [x] The change is implemented in both the TypeScript CLI and the Rust `pacquet/` port, or the description notes what still needs porting. - [x] Added a changeset (`pnpm changeset`) if this PR changes any published package. Keep it short and written for pnpm users — it becomes a release note. - [x] Added or updated tests. - [x] Updated the documentation if needed. --- Written by an agent (opencode, glm-5.2). ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Added install-time warnings for `pnpm.overrides` selectors that match no dependency. * Warnings are grouped into a single `[WARN]` line (sorted selectors, singular/plural) after `resolution_done`, including pnpr-server installs. * **Configuration** * Added `warnUnusedOverrides` (default: `true`), the `warn-unused-overrides` key, and `WARN_UNUSED_OVERRIDES` / `pnpm_config_warn_unused_overrides`. * You can disable via `warnUnusedOverrides: false` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`. * **Bug Fixes** * Selector text is sanitized to prevent terminal/control-character spoofing. * Unused-override detection runs only during full lockfile reanalysis; frozen/cached installs may skip it. #6185 ## Summary Adds an **Appshots**-style global hotkey that captures the **frontmost macOS window** — a screenshot *and* the window's text — and sends it straight into the active agent as context, replicating the killer feature of the Codex Mac app. You're working in another app (browser, Figma, a failing GUI, a Slack thread), you press one hotkey, and the agent you're running in cmux instantly gets full visual **and** textual context — no manual screenshot → save → drag → re-describe loop. ## What's implemented **Trigger** — a new system-wide shortcut `sendAppshot` (default **⌃⌥⌘A**) registered through the existing `SystemWideHotkeyController` (Carbon `RegisterEventHotKey`), so it fires even when cmux isn't frontmost. Fully customizable in **Settings → Keyboard Shortcuts** and `~/.config/cmux/cmux.json`, exactly like `globalSearch`. **Capture** — the frontmost window's image via **ScreenCaptureKit** (`SCScreenshotManager`) plus its text via the **Accessibility API** (an `AXUIElement` walk, budgeted). Both are written to temp files under `cmux-appshots/`. Degrades gracefully: image-only when Accessibility is missing, text-only when Screen Recording is missing. **Routing (60-second recency rule)** — consecutive appshots stack onto the same thread; an appshot within 60s of interacting with an agent appends to that agent; otherwise a new workspace/thread is started. The capture is delivered as a **single-line message that references the saved files by path**, which: - works with every terminal agent (Claude Code, Codex, …) regardless of pasted-image support — sidesteps #6039; - never embeds newlines, so a single Return submits it cleanly to a TUI agent instead of executing fragments line-by-line; - keeps large Accessibility text out of the TUI (the agent `Read`s the file). Delivery deliberately does **not** steal focus from the frontmost app, so you can fire several appshots in a row from the same external window. **Permissions** — `NSScreenCaptureUsageDescription` added; a first-run prompt opens the right System Settings panes and registers cmux with TCC; and a new **Settings → Appshots** section shows live Screen Recording + Accessibility status with **re-check / re-grant** affordances. ## Architecture / testing - Pure, Foundation-only logic (`AppshotModel.swift`): the single-line prompt formatter and the recency-routing decision — both covered by `AppshotRoutingTests`. - Orchestration, capture, AX, permissions, and delivery live in `AppshotController.swift` (capture runs off the main actor; recency state + delivery stay on the main actor). - One shared action path: the shortcut, the settings affordance, and the dispatch all flow through `AppshotController` / `KeyboardShortcutSettings`. ## Scope note This PR ships the customizable Carbon-based global hotkey (the path that's "customizable via `KeyboardShortcutSettings`"). The issue's headline *double-tap-both-⌘* default gesture needs a separate global modifier-monitor subsystem (Input Monitoring) and is intentionally left as a follow-up; the hotkey is the substance and is fully rebindable today. ## Localization All new user-facing strings (shortcut label, injected prompt, permission alert, settings section) added to `Resources/Localizable.xcstrings` with **en + ja** (matching the sibling shortcut labels and the project's documented policy). Web docs use inline en/ja in `cmux-shortcuts.ts`. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Adds a system-wide `sendAppshot` hotkey (default ⌃⌥⌘A) that captures the frontmost window (screenshot + Accessibility text) and stages a sanitized, single-line message into the right agent using a 60s recency rule, routing to the active agent and opening a new workspace only when no terminal exists (Fixes #6185). Adds Settings → Appshots for live Screen Recording + Accessibility checks with localized prompts and re-check/redirect actions. - New Features - Global shortcut `sendAppshot`, configurable in Settings → Keyboard Shortcuts and `~/.config/cmux/cmux.json`; single-stroke with a primary modifier; works when cmux isn’t frontmost. - Capture via `ScreenCaptureKit` + Accessibility; artifacts saved under temp `cmux-appshots/` with bounded eviction; AX walk and PNG encode/disk writes run off the main thread with strict time/size/timeouts. - Routing: 60s recency (stack or append to recent agent; else fall back to the active agent pane); delivery stages a single-line prompt referencing file paths, frames content as untrusted, and doesn’t auto-submit or steal focus. - Settings → Appshots shows live Screen Recording + Accessibility status with “Open System Settings” and “Re-check.” Adds localized `NSScreenCaptureUsageDescription`. - Bug Fixes - Bind Accessibility text to the captured window only when the frame match is unique; otherwise fall back to the focused window. - Treat `sendAppshot` as a system-wide hotkey across Settings and dispatch; reject chords and Shift-only with primary-modifier messaging; exclude all system-wide hotkeys from bare-start routing. - Record the chosen route after a staged send so subsequent appshots append to the correct agent. - Sanitization/stability: strip control characters and shell metacharacters (including `!`); enforce a single 2s AX time budget; cap scanned windows/children; bound all AX IPC with a process-wide per-call timeout and ranged/limited reads; guard AX title/description with bounded CFString bridging; never materialize unbounded AX strings; move PNG encode and file writes off the main thread; gate debug logs behind `#if DEBUG`; tighten trust boundaries around captured content. Written for commit 98497a7fc6145186c411ba3a608be11e57d3c950. Summary will update on new commits. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Added an **Appshots** settings section showing Screen Recording and Accessibility status, with “re-check permissions” and links to System Settings. * Introduced a new system-wide hotkey (default **Ctrl+Option+Cmd+A**) to capture the frontmost window (screenshot + accessible text when available) and send it to the active agent, with automatic fallback to a new workspace/thread when needed. * **Bug Fixes** * Improved permission prompting/handling and added stronger single-line sanitization for captured app/window text. * **Tests** * Added automated tests for prompt formatting/sanitization and 60-second recency routing behavior. There is an active complaint. The draft neither names the organisation nor quotes the correspondence, supplies case specifics or asserts that an error has been established. Phil subsequently supplied the feeling of injustice, his self-description as a generally law-abiding, tax-paying citizen and the fact that similar encounters have left a bad taste before. The new paragraph is grounded in that account. Possible internal divisions between correspondence, enforcement and complaints are explicitly framed as Phil's speculation. The article stays with the experience of not knowing how a challenge affects action under way. ## Editorial review Read `EDITORIAL.md`, `VOICE.md`, `AUTOMATION.md`, the author-language and concrete-detail learnings, and four recent posts. The conversational first draft was discarded as article copy because of stacked single-line paragraphs, a staged conclusion and unsupported claims about internal operations. Motivation The current multi-output generation (controlled by `num_outputs_per_prompt`) assembles all outputs into a single batch at the denoising stage level. While functional for a few models (e.g., Flux, Wan-T2V), this approach has three significant problems( thanks to @MikukuOvO ): 1. **Poor model generalization.** Every model must be individually adapted to handle batched multi-output execution inside its denoising loop. Models that were not explicitly modified fail in various ways: - Qwen-Image — text/latent batch dimension mismatch. - Z-Image — model code hardcodes single-sample assumptions. - Hunyuan3D — code explicitly rejects batch size > 1. - Helios / GLM-Image — `batch_size=1` is hardcoded throughout; the entire processing path never accounts for batch > 1 and would require a full rewrite to support it. 2. **Excessive memory consumption.** Internal batch size equals `num_outputs_per_prompt`, linearly scaling activation memory. This causes OOM in RL rollout scenarios that require many outputs, while providing no throughput benefit since denoising is already compute-bound on a single sample. 3. **Training–inference inconsistency risk in RL.** Running with `batch_size = N` during rollout may trigger different operator implementations or kernel dispatches compared to training, risking numerical divergence in RL reward signals. This PR introduces a **sequential per-output execution** strategy at the **executor layer**. By looping over outputs at the orchestration level instead of inside each model's denoising code. ## Modifications ### Core Design: Stage-Level `requires_per_output_execution` Property A new boolean property `requires_per_output_execution` is added to the `PipelineStage` base class (default `False`). Stages that are seed-/noise-dependent override it to `True`: | Stage | `requires_per_output_execution` | Rationale | |--------------------------|:-------------------------------:|-----------| | `LatentPreparationStage` | `True` | Generates unique noise per output | | `DenoisingStage` | `True` | Iterative denoising is seed-specific | | `DecodingStage` | `True` | VAE decode operates on per-output latents | | `GlmImageBeforeDenoisingStage` | `True` | Model-specific pre-denoising prep that is output-dependent | | All other stages (e.g., text encoding) | `False` | Shared across all outputs | ### Executor-Level Sequential Loop The execution flow in both `PipelineExecutor` and `ParallelExecutor` is extended with a three-phase strategy when `num_outputs_per_prompt > 1`: 1. **Phase 1 — Shared stages**: Stages before the first `requires_per_output_execution = True` stage (e.g., text encoding) execute **once**. 2. **Phase 2 — Per-output loop**: Stages from the first per-output stage onward are executed **N times** sequentially, each with an independent `Req` copy carrying its own seed/generator and `num_outputs_per_prompt = 1`. 3. **Phase 3 — Merge**: The N `OutputBatch` results are concatenated back into a single `OutputBatch`. Key helper functions added to `pipeline_executor.py`: - **`_split_stages_by_per_output(stages)`** — Partitions stages into shared and per-output groups. Once the first per-output stage is encountered, all subsequent stages are treated as per-output to preserve execution order. - **`_prepare_single_output_batch(batch, output_index)`** — Deep-copies the batch, selects the correct generator/seed for the given output index, clears latents, and sets `num_outputs_per_prompt = 1`. - **`_merge_output_batches(output_batches)`** — Concatenates output tensors from N runs into a single `(N, ...)` tensor. ### Invasiveness & Maintainability - **Minimal invasiveness**: No changes to any model forward passes or denoising loops. For models with custom pre-denoising stages, only a one-line property override is needed. - **Backward compatible**: When `num_outputs_per_prompt ≤ 1` (default), the original `_execute()` path is taken — zero overhead. - **Easy to extend**: Supporting a new stage requires only a one-line property override. ## Accuracy Tests With this implementation, the following models all correctly support single-prompt multi-output generation **without any model-specific modifications**: | Model | Status | Notes | |-------|--------|-------| | **Flux** | ✅ Pass | Previously supported (batched); now works sequentially | | **Qwen-Image** | ✅ Pass | Previously failed (batch dim mismatch) | | **Z-Image** | ✅ Pass | Previously failed (single-sample hardcoded) | | **Wan-T2V** | ✅ Pass | Previously supported (batched); now works sequentially | | **Wan-I2V** | ✅ Pass | Now works with sequential execution | | **GLM-Image** | ✅ Pass | Previously failed (hardcoded `batch_size=1`); fixed by marking `GlmImageBeforeDenoisingStage` as per-output | Each model was tested with `num_outputs_per_prompt = 4` and results were visually verified for correctness and diversity (different seeds producing different outputs). The screenshots below demonstrate the tests conducted on qwen-image. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Benchmarked on **Flux (FLUX.1-dev)** on a single **H200** GPU with `num_outputs_per_prompt = 4`. **Command:** ```bash sglang generate \ --model-path black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-dev \ --prompt "A curious raccoon sitting on a mossy rock in a sunlit forest, photorealistic, 8k" \ --width 1024 --height 1024 \ --num-outputs-per-prompt 4 \ --num-inference-steps 28 \ --guidance-scale 3.5 \ --save-output --output-path ./test_outputs/flux1 \ --log-level debug --warmup ``` **Results:** | Metric | Batched (before) | Sequential (after) | Delta | |--------|:-----------------:|:-------------------:|:-----:| | DiT time | 15.2041 s | 15.4286 s | +1.4% | | Peak GPU memory | 57,104 MB | **32,042 MB** | **↓ 43.9%** | The screenshot below shows the execution log before the modification. The screenshot below shows the modified execution log. **Key takeaways:** - The DiT (denoising transformer) time difference of +1.4% is within normal variance on H200 and does not represent a meaningful regression. - Peak memory reduction **scales with the number of outputs** — since activations are never held for more than one output at a time, memory stays constant regardless of N. With N=4, peak VRAM dropped from 57.1 GB to 32.0 GB (**↓ 43.9%**). - Critically, the batched approach **fails with OOM** at higher output counts, whereas the sequential approach can handle **arbitrarily large N** with the same memory footprint as a single generation. This makes it viable for RL rollout scenarios that require many outputs per prompt. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Those are CUDA **Driver API** symbols from `libcuda.so`, which ships with the NVIDIA driver — present on every real GPU machine (which is why the identical build recipe worked on the rented pod) but absent on GitHub's GPU-less runners. ## Fix NVIDIA's devel base images ship link-time stubs at `/usr/local/cuda/lib64/stubs/` for exactly this case. The build stage now sets `LIBRARY_PATH` to that directory, which covers both CUDA compiles (the llama.cpp cmake link and the `llama-cpp-python` wheel build). At runtime the pod's real driver provides `libcuda.so`; the stub never leaves the build stage (the runtime stage copies only `build/bin` and `/opt/wheels`). One line plus the why-comment. Description I noticed unexpected formatting changes in a recent PR: `ChatInput.tsx` and `types/ai-assistant.ts` were reformatted with no logic change. I couldn't drop them, because prettier runs when I commit and puts them straight back. I asked Claude to run prettier across every tracked file it covers, so hopefully this can unite things in future PRs: ``` git ls-files -z | grep -zE '\.(js|ts|tsx|jsx|md)$' \ | xargs -0 npx --prefix assets prettier --config .prettierrc \ --ignore-path .prettierignore --write ``` That's the same prettier invocation as the pre-commit hook in `config/dev.exs:176-180`, over every tracked file rather than just the staged ones. ## Validation steps n/a: Formatting only, no behaviour change: line wrapping, union-type indentation, and trailing whitespace in a benchmarking sample. ## Additional notes for the reviewer I don't know how this drifted, and I'd rather we agree the process than guess. 1. What is our prettier process? Nothing is written down: no mention of it in CLAUDE.md or CONTRIBUTING.md. 2. What should run on commit, and is it running for everyone? The hook installs itself as a side effect of compiling in dev, so it's easy not to have. 3. Should CI check formatting instead of, or as well as, the hook? 4. Which file types should it cover? Today it's `.js .ts .tsx .jsx .md`. Adding json/css/yml would touch 21 more files, and some of those shouldn't be reformatted (`test/fixtures/*.json`, the generated `priv/static/manifest.json`, and `priv/static/workflow-api.yaml`, which prettier can't parse). ## AI Usage Please disclose whether you've used AI anywhere in this PR (it's cool, we just want to know!): - [x] I have used Claude Code - [ ] I have used another model - [ ] I have not used AI You can read more details in our [Responsible AI Policy](https://www.openfn.org/ai#pull-request-templates) ## Pre-submission checklist - [x] I have performed an AI review of my code (we recommend using `/review` with Claude Code) - [ ] I have implemented and tested all related **authorization policies**. Problem `kasb upgrade` gave no feedback until it printed its final JSON document, so a person at a terminal could not tell whether it was querying releases, downloading, verifying, or installing. ## Change `kasb upgrade` and `kasb upgrade --check` write one plain-text line per stage to **stderr, only when stderr is an interactive terminal** (`std::io::IsTerminal`): ``` Checking for the latest kasb release... Downloading kasb 0.6.0 (kasb-0.6.0-win32-x64-msvc.tar.gz, 5.3 MB)... Verifying the release archive... Installing kasb 0.6.0... kasb 0.6.0 is scheduled to replace 0.5.0 after this process exits. ``` - stdout is unchanged: still the single JSON document. Pipes, CI, and agents keep an empty stderr. - Write failures are ignored; progress never fails the upgrade. - Windows reports the replacement as *scheduled*, because the helper can still roll back after exit. Unix reports `Upgraded kasb X to Y.` only after the replacement succeeds. - Stage lines rather than a progress bar: release archives are about 5–6 MB, so the missing signal is which stage is running, not byte counts. - `docs/specs/kasb-standards-v1.md` and `crates/kasb-cli/README.md` record this as the one exception to the parseable-diagnostics and empty-stderr rules. The root README mentions it. ## Validation - `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `bun run contracts:check`, and `cargo test --workspace --locked` pass locally on Windows. - New tests cover the stage sequence for up-to-date, check-available, cancelled-after-metadata-download, and size formatting. `progress_reports_an_applied_upgrade` is `cfg(unix)`, so only CI runs it. - Not covered: there is no test of the Windows "scheduled" line, and I did not watch a real managed upgrade end to end because that needs a newer published release. - `bun run test:installers` fails locally with a path-with-spaces error in `install.sh` under Git Bash. Why External verifiers check a deployed `vllm-proxy-rs` digest by rebuilding the pinned source commit with `ENABLE_NV_ATTESTATION_SDK=1 SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=0 bash build-image.sh` and comparing the OCI manifest digest. That holds on the day CI builds a commit, but not necessarily later. The builder stage installs its toolchain from the live Ubuntu archive (gcc-11, binutils, libc6-dev, clang-14, libclang, libssl-dev), rustup comes from `sh.rustup.rs`, and the NVIDIA keyring is downloaded without a checksum. The binary contains natively compiled code (aws-lc-sys, ring, secp256k1-sys, bindgen via libclang), so an Ubuntu toolchain update changes its bytes and a pinned commit quietly stops reproducing. `reproducible-build.yml` builds twice on the same day, so it cannot catch this. This PR makes the builder stage hermetic, using the same approach as cloud-api. The runtime stage only gains one `COPY --from=builder` line; replacing the runtime base is a separate PR. ## What changed - **Snapshot apt with exact pins (builder).** apt reads `https://snapshot.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/20260924T000000Z` (`jammy`, `jammy-updates`, `jammy-security`), set once in `ARG UBUNTU_SNAPSHOT`. Every package in the new `pinned-packages-builder.txt` (212 entries) is held at its exact version with `Pin-Priority: 1001`. The requested package set is the same as before. - **CA bootstrap outside the builder.** The snapshot is https-only and `ubuntu:22.04` ships no CA certificates. A throwaway `ca-bootstrap` stage installs `ca-certificates` from the regular archive, and the builder only bind-mounts its CA bundle for its first `apt-get update`/`install` (`-o Acquire::https::CAInfo=...`). The builder's own `ca-certificates` comes from the snapshot. I first tried bootstrapping inside the builder (what cloud-api's runtime stage does), but that leaks live versions: it installs `openssl` at whatever the live archive serves (today `3.0.2-0ubuntu1.29`), and the pinned install never touches it again. A newer live `ca-certificates` would also need a downgrade, which `apt-get -y` refuses. Because the resolved package list ships in the image, either case would change an old commit's digest. - **Resolved list in the image.** The builder records `dpkg -l` as sorted `name=version` lines, and the runtime stage copies it to `/app/pinned-packages-builder.txt`. Local (non-push) runs of `build-image.sh` extract it to `pinned-packages-builder.resolved.txt` and print a warning if it differs from the committed file. `*.resolved.txt` is git- and docker-ignored. A CI guard for this diff belongs to the CI follow-up. - **rustup.** `rustup-init` 1.29.1 is downloaded from `static.rust-lang.org/rustup/archive/1.29.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/rustup-init` and checked against a committed sha256 (`dda72343…`, which matches both the published `.sha256` and my own hash of the binary). It replaces piping `sh.rustup.rs` into `sh`. The toolchain stays 1.93.0. I did not add a `rust-toolchain.toml`: `ci.yml` installs `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable`, and a toolchain file would change which compiler it runs. - **NVIDIA keyring.** `cuda-keyring_1.1-1_all.deb` is checked against a committed sha256 (`d93190d5…`) before `dpkg -i`. `libnvat`/`libnvat-dev` stay pinned to `LIBNVAT_VERSION`. Residual risk, noted in the header: NVIDIA's repo has no snapshot service. It still lists every libnvat release so far (1.0.0 to 1.2.2); if it ever dropped ours, older commits would fail to build rather than drift. - **Docs and CI filter.** The Dockerfile header now describes the build contract, each hermetic input, the residual risks and how to bump each input. `reproducible-build.yml` adds the pin file to its push `paths` filter, since the file is a new bind source. No new env var or build arg is required: every new `ARG` defaults to the CI value inside the Dockerfile. `ENABLE_NV_ATTESTATION_SDK=0` still builds, and the output is still a single-manifest `./oci.tar`. ## How to bump - `UBUNTU_SNAPSHOT`: use a timestamp in the past (`YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ`). The service also answers for future timestamps, whose content is not frozen yet. Check that `dists/{jammy,jammy-updates,jammy-security}/InRelease` exist under it, then regenerate the pin file. - `pinned-packages-builder.txt`: run `: > pinned-packages-builder.txt`, then `ENABLE_NV_ATTESTATION_SDK=1 ./build-image.sh`, then `cp pinned-packages-builder.resolved.txt pinned-packages-builder.txt`. Rebuild and check that `diff -u pinned-packages-builder.txt pinned-packages-builder.resolved.txt` is empty. Always generate it with the SDK flag on, since that set is a superset of the flag-off set. Regenerate after changing the snapshot, `LIBNVAT_VERSION`, the base image or the install lists. - `RUSTUP_VERSION` / `RUSTUP_INIT_SHA256`: take the version from `https://static.rust-lang.org/rustup/release-stable.toml`, hash the archived binary yourself and compare it with the published `rustup-init.sha256`. - `CUDA_KEYRING_SHA256`: `sha256sum` of the new `.deb`. - `LIBNVAT_VERSION`: a version listed in the NVIDIA repo index, then regenerate the pin file. ## Verification - **Pins.** On buffy (x86_64, BuildKit v0.20.2), a build with an empty pin file resolved 212 packages, committed here as `pinned-packages-builder.txt`. The pinned rebuild resolved the same list (`diff -u` empty). An `ENABLE_NV_ATTESTATION_SDK=0` build resolved 168 packages, all present in the pin file with the same versions. - **The pins are enforced.** With the generated preferences file, `apt-cache policy` shows priority 1001 on the pinned versions, including arch-qualified names such as `libc6:amd64`. Pinning one package below the snapshot's version makes the install fail rather than resolve differently. - **Contract command.** Fresh clone of `70fe98d`, `env -i PATH="$PATH" HOME="$HOME" ENABLE_NV_ATTESTATION_SDK=1 SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=0 bash build-image.sh`, digest read with `tar -xOf oci.tar index.json | jq -r .manifests[0].digest`: | Build | Host | Digest | |---|---|---| | local 1 (378 s) | buffy | `sha256:e547dc551b30ec378c64e8955b9688c275038444e71719ef28acca4eb13bbd7f` | | local 2 (283 s) | buffy | `sha256:e547dc551b30ec378c64e8955b9688c275038444e71719ef28acca4eb13bbd7f` | | local 3 (284 s, after CI finished) | buffy | `sha256:e547dc551b30ec378c64e8955b9688c275038444e71719ef28acca4eb13bbd7f` | | `build.yml`, [run 35993985629](https://github.com/nearai/inference-proxy/actions/runs/35993985629) | gpu04 | `sha256:e547dc551b30ec378c64e8955b9688c275038444e71719ef28acca4eb13bbd7f` | | `reproducible-build.yml` build 1 and 2, [run 35993983218](https://github.com/nearai/inference-proxy/actions/runs/35993983218) (green) | gpu02 | `sha256:e547dc551b30ec378c64e8955b9688c275038444e71719ef28acca4eb13bbd7f` (both) | The provenance attestation for that digest names commit `70fe98d` and `build.yml@refs/heads/feat/hermetic-builder`. On every host the resolved package list matched the committed pins. - **Smoke test** on the image loaded from local build 1's `oci.tar`: ``` $ docker run --rm --entrypoint ldd /app/vllm-proxy-rs | grep -E 'nvat|ssl|not found' libnvat.so.1 => /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnvat.so.1 (0x...) $ docker run --rm --entrypoint /app/vllm-proxy-rs Error: MODEL_NAME environment variable is required ``` The full `ldd` output has no `not found`. The binary does not link libssl at all (`NEEDED`: libnvat, libgcc_s, libm, libc, ld-linux), the same as earlier published images. ## Notes - The runtime stage still installs libnvat's apt dependencies from the vLLM base's regular sources, so the image as a whole is not hermetic until the runtime-stage PR lands. - When checking a digest by hand, clone with umask 022. `gpu_evidence_worker.py` is copied with its checkout mode, so a group-writable checkout (umask 002) gives a different digest. CI's checkout gives 644. This predates this PR. Still no model — this is the coverage half, measured with a stand-in narrator so the result is structural rather than a claim about prose quality. ## The wall, in its precise shape Measured on the loop the product actually has — leave for a week, come back, read the briefing, twenty times over: ```text table only: 207 lines, 80 distinct (61% repeat) Pressure is rising 18 lines / 3 distinct (83% repeat) The pressure peaked 17 lines / 3 distinct (82% repeat) Something was lost 17 lines / 3 distinct (82% repeat) ``` Exactly three phrasings each, because there are three troubles per seed and one written line per stage. #299's seam narrated only the most recent consequence, so those other entries stayed on the table. ## After ```text narrated: 207 lines, 124 distinct (40% repeat) Pressure is rising 18 lines / 18 distinct (0% repeat) The pressure peaked 17 lines / 17 distinct (0% repeat) Something was lost 17 lines / 17 distinct (0% repeat) ``` **61% → 40% on the return path, and the three lines that were the wall now repeat not at all.** ## How The projection decides which Events a return digest shows; that list is now extracted as `digest_events` and handed to the narrator, so what gets put into words can never drift from what gets read. `return_digest_items` is built from the same call. The cost budget is unchanged and now says what it always meant: **a return is one request, however many lines it puts on the page.** `Narrator::narrate_all` carries the whole briefing; a narrator backed by a model overrides it to ask once, and the default implementation asks line by line, which is what a local or scripted narrator wants. ## Tests The once-per-return test now asserts the property that actually matters — one *request*, and more than one line put into the World's own words, never more than the digest shows. A new test asserts the briefing keeps no table line for an entry the World already has words for. Please describe.**

I am using the SMS authenticator for sending auth tokens via Telegram and Signal messages. With the Generic web-hook interface and a small Node-RED flow linking to a Telegram or a Signal API endpoint, this basically works well. For Telegram, a custom prompt explaining the user how to get their Telegram ID (which is used instead of the phone number) is needed, but that is no problem due to the flexibility of authentik's prompts.

However, there are a couple of rough edges that might be improved upon, especially for non-technical end-users:

1. It is currently possible to setup multiple SMS authenticators per user, such as, both a Telegram and a Signal account, for instance. Only a single one of these is presented upon login, though, seemingly at random. Since the label is always "SMS (Tokens sent via SMS)", the user cannot tell which one it is. This is a minor point if you have both (or all) messenger accounts on the same device anyway, but might be undesirable when the user has, say, a personal and a work device with separate accounts and can only use one of them at some point.
2. Setting up SMS authenticators for different user accounts with the same effective Signal or Telegram destination is only possible with a workaround: For Signal, which uses a phone number, that same phone number needs to be formatted slightly differently for each use, e.g. "+491234567890" vs. "+49 123 4567890" or "0123 4567890" (for a German phone number). For Telegram, one might add spurious characters to the ID, which are stripped by the external API glue code (e.g., "123456789" vs. "123456789x"). This is unnecessarily cumbersome. My specific use case is a regular user account and the akadmin account, both of which I would like to secure with 2FA using the same messenger account. Other cases of multiple-account users seem reasonable as well.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

For 1., my favored solution would be for all SMS authenticator instances to show up on the selection page. Instead of just "SMS", the user-configurable name of the specific instance should be shown to be able to tell them apart. The default being "SMS Device", this would not change much for the current use as a (unique) SMS authenticator, but would allow users to rename their devices to "Signal on +491234567890" or "Signal work phone" etc.

For 2., my favored solution would be to simply allow re-use of already-in-use phone numbers.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

For 1., the obvious alternative is to disallow multiple instances of the SMS authenticator service per user. This should then be enforced at the point of configuration, i.e., trying to setup a second SMS authenticator should be prevented with an error message like, "You need to remove your existing SMS authenticator before configuring a new device". A similar result might be achieved with an appropriate authentik policy, but this shouldn't be necessary for a condition that is forbidden in any case.

For 2., if multiple use of the (exact) same phone number string is not desired, a more informative error message should be given. Currently, trying to enter a duplicate phone number at the configuration stage results in the following runtime error

#### 'AuthenticatorSMSChallengeResponse' object has no attribute '_errors'

```
    ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

```

I do not see any advantages of these alternatives, though. 

**Additional context**

This is probably not specific to Signal and Telegram, which I happen to be using. Furthermore, similar issues might apply to cases of multiple instances of TOTP or Static Token authenticators per user, but I have not tried that.

I am using authentik version 2023.8.1.

description**

Sometimes, Git decides to show multiple unrelated changes together as a single hunk, or perhaps you'd like to have more control about splitting out several sets of unrelated but co-developed changes when committing them.

Right now it is possible to stage individual lines by selecting them first, and then hitting the "Stage Lines" button that appears below the normal "Stage Hunk". However, I only discovered that this functionality existed at all while starting to write up this issue after spending a week wishing it did, and only after the Github related-issue search recommended Issue #206 to me.

TLDR: It's hard to discover that it's possible to stage/unstage individual lines

**Preferred solution**
To make it more discoverable, it would be awesome if hovering over the line numbers shows a button/widget over the line number that, when clicked, would stage/unstage the offending line.

**Alternatives**
If it's not feasible to implement or too distracting, I could live with an entry in a right click menu that appears when clicking on part of the offending line. That's what Git GUI had (i.e. the TK/TCL tool I've been using for many years until last week, when I started using SublimeMerge as I didn't have install permissions on my work box;  BTW, I'm really pleased happy that this tool exists in the first place - being forced to use the command line only was like developing with one hand tied behind my back while juggling knives!)

Home Assistant Version

2025.1.5

### Bambu Lab Integration Version

2.0.41

### Describe the bug

The camera stopped working when this version was applied. Says streaming, but window is black.  I saw in notes work was done for IP address from MQTT. Looking at my device attributes, the IP Address field in HA is blank. So if it's substituting the blank over the one in the config, that would explain this. 

While checking settings, printer confirmed on original IP, I clicked the Configure button and when I save I now get "Failed to connect. Check provided settings." even though all the values (IP, code, hours) are correct. 

I restored a backup and camera is back and Configure button works. 

I believe the new address logic is breaking things perhaps.

### To Reproduce

Install update.
Go to devices and pick integration and then device.
Camera is black.
Go to integration, click configure button.
Fields are prefilled, verify, save. 
Failure message.

### Expected Behaviour

Camera and config should use the supplied IP if the MQTT IP is blank, or logically, in LAN only mode use the static address in the config.

### What device are you using?

P1S

What changed

The root coordinator still owned Tempo-specific request validation, target filtering, and workflow-row construction. This PR moves that pure planner into `internal/coordinator/tempoplanner` and wires `workflow-coordinator` to the child `WorkPlanner`.

The parent coordinator still owns scheduling order, the clock-derived plan key, tenant and egress filtering, durable admission, retries, and telemetry. The move adds no network or database work, queue, goroutine, lock, lease, or runtime setting. Summary

`main/dataset/mano2dexhand.py` uses `idx[-1]` to extract the stage number when constructing the retargeting output filename for OakInk-v2. Since `idx[-1]` returns the **last character** of the string rather than the full substring after `@`, any task ID with a two-digit stage number (e.g., `01857@12`) silently truncates to a single digit (`2`), colliding with the single-digit stage of the same sequence. This causes **two independent failures** during training.

---

### Root Cause

**`main/dataset/mano2dexhand.py`, lines 501 and 509:**

```python
# Line 501 — dataset_type == "oakink2"
dump_path = f"data/retargeting/OakInk-v2/mano2{str(dexhand)}/"\
            f"{os.path.split(demo_data['data_path'][0])[-1].replace('.pkl', f'@{idx[-1]}.pkl')}"

# Line 509 — dataset_type == "oakink2_mirrored"
dump_path = f"data/retargeting/OakInk-v2-mirrored/mano2{str(dexhand)}/"\
            f"{os.path.split(demo_data['data_path'][0])[-1].replace('.pkl', f'@{idx[-1]}.pkl')}"
```

`idx` is a string like `"01857@12"`. `idx[-1]` is `'2'`, not `'12'`.

**The training loader uses the correct stage number** (`main/dataset/oakink2_dataset_dexhand_rh.py`, line 220):

```python
opt_path = os.path.join(
    OPT_INSPIRE_PATH, os.path.split(self.data_pathes[idx])[-1].replace(".pkl", f"@{stage}.pkl")
)
```

The write path and read path are **asymmetric** — the writer truncates the stage, the reader does not.

---

### Minimal Reproduction

```python
# Demonstrates filename collision caused by idx[-1]
task_ids = ["01857@2", "01857@12", "01857@10", "01857@20"]

print("Buggy  (idx[-1]):")
for idx in task_ids:
    print(f"  {idx!r:15} -> @{idx[-1]}.pkl")

print("\nCorrect (idx.split('@')[1]):")
for idx in task_ids:
    print(f"  {idx!r:15} -> @{idx.split('@')[1]}.pkl")
```

Output:
```
Buggy  (idx[-1]):
  '01857@2'       -> @2.pkl
  '01857@12'      -> @2.pkl    ← collision with stage 2
  '01857@10'      -> @0.pkl    ← collision with stage 0
  '01857@20'      -> @0.pkl    ← collision with stage 0

Correct (idx.split('@')[1]):
  '01857@2'       -> @2.pkl
  '01857@12'      -> @12.pkl
  '01857@10'      -> @10.pkl
  '01857@20'      -> @20.pkl
```

---

### Impact

This bug causes **two simultaneous failures**:

#### Failure 1 — Single-digit stages load wrong retargeted data during training (silent data corruption)

When retargeting is run for stage `01857@12`, the output is written to `@2.pkl`, **overwriting** the correctly retargeted data for stage `01857@2`. During training, the dataset loader requests `@2.pkl` for stage 2, but the file now contains the retargeted DOF positions and wrist poses for stage 12 (a different action, possibly a different object). The mismatch between the demo trajectory and the RSI initialization is never detected — there is no checksum, no shape mismatch, and no error message.

#### Failure 2 — All stages ≥ 10 silently fall back to zero initialization during training

The training loader constructs the correct path (e.g., `@12.pkl`) for stage 12, but that file is never written by `mano2dexhand.py`. Since `load_retargeted_data` falls back to zero DOF initialization when the file is missing, **all stages ≥ 10 effectively receive no retargeting**, defeating the purpose of the preprocessing step and likely degrading convergence.

---

### Fix

Replace `idx[-1]` with `idx.split('@')[1]` in both lines:

**`main/dataset/mano2dexhand.py`:**

```python
# Before (line 501)
dump_path = f"data/retargeting/OakInk-v2/mano2{str(dexhand)}/"\
            f"{os.path.split(demo_data['data_path'][0])[-1].replace('.pkl', f'@{idx[-1]}.pkl')}"

# After
stage_str = idx.split('@')[1]
dump_path = f"data/retargeting/OakInk-v2/mano2{str(dexhand)}/"\
            f"{os.path.split(demo_data['data_path'][0])[-1].replace('.pkl', f'@{stage_str}.pkl')}"
```

```python
# Before (line 509)
dump_path = f"data/retargeting/OakInk-v2-mirrored/mano2{str(dexhand)}/"\
            f"{os.path.split(demo_data['data_path'][0])[-1].replace('.pkl', f'@{idx[-1]}.pkl')}"

# After
dump_path = f"data/retargeting/OakInk-v2-mirrored/mano2{str(dexhand)}/"\
            f"{os.path.split(demo_data['data_path'][0])[-1].replace('.pkl', f'@{stage_str}.pkl')}"
```

> **Note:** Any previously generated retargeting results for OakInk-v2 sequences with stages ≥ 10, as well as any single-digit stages that were overwritten, must be regenerated after applying this fix.

---

What

Field Team Program Phase 0 item 3 — **PR C of the tech-lines plan** (PR A #3934 capabilities editor, PR B #3936 names + roster are merged). Each field technician can hold one Waves Twilio line; texts and calls to it reach that tech, and the office never loses sight of it.

The number is **(941) 352-9161** (bought by Adam 2026-09-07). Its Twilio side is already done by a parallel session (voice/SMS/status webhooks identical to the location lines, customer profile + trust products, A2P messaging service) — this PR is the portal side only.

**Ships DARK: `GATE_TECH_LINES` unset.** Read at call time by the number registry — no redeploy to flip, unset is the live kill. Off, the line is reported exactly like an unassigned office number (inbound is never dropped; today, before this PR, texts to it are dropped as "unmanaged" and calls log as location `unknown`).

## How it works (gate on)

| Surface | Behavior |
|---|---|
| Registry | `fieldTech` bucket in `server/config/twilio-numbers.js`; `findByNumber` → `type: 'tech_line'`; listed in `allNumbers` (stats, webhook scripts), owned/internal (never keyed as a lead) |
| Who answers | `technicians.twilio_number` — Team tab picker on Add/Edit, shown in the roster. One holder per line: in-trx check under the technicians table lock + partial unique index; `409 TECH_LINE_TAKEN`; `400` for a number outside the registry; `''` clears |
| Inbound text | Office bell / inbox thread (keyed by the line as `our_endpoint_id`) / owner forward exactly as a location line, **plus** a `tech_line_sms` tech-home card + one-line push for the holder (`server/services/tech-line.js`). No auto-reply ever fires from a tech line |
| Inbound call | Holder's cell rings first, alone, 20 s, with the press-1 screen (`<Dial action=…/call-complete?stage=tech_line>`); an unaccepted leg continues into the office forward list from `/call-complete`; voicemail / AI backstop only after both. No holder, holder not assignable, or no cell on file → office list as today. **Office lines are byte-identical** (action URL unchanged when no stage) |
| Customer card | `GET /api/card/:token` phone + `contact.vcf` TEL carry the line when the card's tech holds one; office number otherwise |
| Tech home | `TextCard` for `tech_line_sms`: sender, body (or "N photos"), kept until **Got it**, shares the 2-card cap with visit notices; feed orders it with visit notices (bucket 2) |
| Communications | `ALL_NUMBERS` gets a **Tech Lines** group from the shared `client/src/constants/techLines.js` (also feeds the Team tab picker), so the thread label and reply-From picker resolve the line |

Rulings applied (recommendations from the plan, stated as assumptions — say the word and either is a one-line change):
- **Call ring order = tech cell → office list → voicemail** (sequential; a simul-ring would be adding the cell to the office list instead).
- **Automated visit texts never send from the tech line**; replying/calling *from* the line out of the tech portal is a later PR.
- Who-answered attribution for a tech who presses 1 uses the existing `WAVES_CSR_NUMBER_MAP` — add the tech's cell there (runbook step 4).

`````markdown
### Issue 1
frontend/src/app/admin/data/spreadsheet-import/components/spreadsheet-import-wizard.tsx:63
A workbook with one tab per institution can no longer use the row-based import path. The wizard now treats every tab as a data section and accepts only one institution per workbook. Admins who previously imported several institutions from one file must split and remap it before importing. Keep a path for those workbooks.

### Issue 2
frontend/src/app/admin/data/spreadsheet-import/utils/template-mapping.ts:80-85
A column mapped from a non-Courses tab into a section linked to courses creates rows without a course name. The wizard now imports those rows, and staging treats a blank `courses` value as every course. A fee or intake can therefore reach the whole catalogue instead of its intended course. Carry the source row’s course link into each generated row.

### Issue 3
frontend/src/app/admin/data/spreadsheet-import/utils/index.ts:195-199
`expandIntakeRow` splits dates at commas as though they were lists. A single date such as `Jan 5, 2026` becomes two values. The import can then make incorrect intakes or skip the row when its lists have different lengths. Keep punctuation within one date separate from list separators.

### Issue 4
backend/src/modules/platform-users/services/platform-users.service.ts:undefined-179
The signup form sends no `email`, so `onboardInstitution` now saves `institutions.email` as `null` even when the owner's address is unused. The owner must enter an email before saving contact details. Use the owner's address when it is available, and leave it unset only when it would collide.

### Issue 5
frontend/src/app/admin/data/spreadsheet-import/components/import-courses-panel.tsx:24
The history panel combines `skipped`, `errors`, and `merged` as if their `row` values refer to the same workbook lines. Dropped rows use the workbook line, but staging errors and merges use positions in the filtered rows sent to the worker. After an earlier row is dropped, the panel can point admins to the wrong line. Keep the original line number with each staged row.

---

For each issue above, determine whether it is valid and should be fixed. If so, fix it directly.
`````

<h3>Summary</h3>

The PR expands spreadsheet imports, adds clearer source filters, and connects extraction data to organization profiles and branches. It also adds portal progress gating while an extraction is running.

- Spreadsheet imports map each section with defaults and leave rows ready for review.
- Business lists show which import seeded each organization.
- Organization profiles show extracted photos and support labelled extra links.
- Owners can turn an extracted campus into an editable branch.
- The business portal shows extraction progress while profile data is being written.
- The organization switcher groups branches beneath their head offices.
- Navigation labels stay readable when a sidebar or list is tight on space.

Why

A core release tag currently builds three image families on hosted runners. Verifier and indexer builds still require unavailable self-hosted runners. The existing hosted workflow should build every required family from the same source revision.

## What changed

- Add `via-verifier` and `via-l1-indexer` to the existing build and manifest matrices. Retain the existing families and EN arm64 build.
- Label images with `org.opencontainers.image.revision` from the actual checkout, not the workflow's `github.sha`.
- Reuse the server Dockerfile’s cargo-chef and mold stages for verifier and indexer. Preserve their runtime stages and binary targets.
- Resolve the release tag once to a commit SHA before matrix checkout. Update the existing operator guide.
- Admit the existing Dockerfiles in `.dockerignore` and their source paths in CI. Preserve the snapshot Dockerfile filter.

## Reuse & Duplication

Extend `build-core-template.yml`. Keep the existing Dockerfiles, contract preparation, caches, registries, and component workflows. No runtime logic changes.

## Performance, Complexity, and Resource Impact

The seven-file diff adds two amd64 builds and their dependency-cache stages. New cache scopes are cold until trusted builds export them. A read-only GitHub cache query reported 24.59 GB of active caches against a configured 20 GB limit; eviction can cause cold rebuilds. The two new scopes have not exported yet. No cache was deleted and no paid capacity setting was changed. Runtime stages and Rust source are unchanged.

## Boundaries and non-goals

This build change is separate from the parser fixes in PRs #392 and #394. The branch is rebased onto merged #394, so the selected release source contains both parser fixes and this build change. An image label records provenance from the trusted build; it is not a reproducible-build attestation.

## How to review

Compare both build matrices with `create_manifest`. Require five families and six platform builds, with arm64 only for the EN. Check that jobs use the same `source_ref` and that manifests consume their platform tags.

## Checks run

The final diff passed `git diff --check`, YAML and matrix checks, CI-filter checks, and both source-revision shell checks. A missing Git checkout failed both blocks without writing an empty revision label. Workflow-only actionlint passed with `-shellcheck=`. Full actionlint exited 1 with the same 31 ShellCheck diagnostics as the base after line-number normalization. Staged and committed-range gitleaks scans passed. The commit signature verified.

Full image builds did not run locally because no Docker daemon was available. Rust suites and structural Rust checks do not apply to these workflow-only paths. The immutable-source fixture passed after moving a disposable tag. Cook and final-build targets match. Hosted CI must establish full-build feasibility before release publication. The local dependency-planner smoke was stopped before Cargo because its isolated VFS storage repeatedly copied the large base layers; it supplies no passing build proof. All six hosted image builds passed at the previous head `7b4655e13e4319bcef38106b194fcd0d0a9e6960`. The combined head `33ebc133581b7ba2078a42933758fbc67b7a6eba` passed workflow actionlint, matrix/YAML checks, committed-diff whitespace checks, gitleaks, and signature verification. Its hosted builds are running. A local harness compiled the exact combined parser source against checksum-verified dependencies: six parser tests passed and two existing tests were ignored. Replay preserved complete messages and deposit identities for 240 retained archive transactions, two bootstrap transactions, and four stored-metadata fixtures. This is retained-corpus evidence, not the required final canonical census.

## Author checklist

- [x] PR title follows Conventional Commits.
- [x] Relevant checks and limits are recorded.
- [x] Runtime tests and structural Rust checks are not applicable.

## Live infrastructure and deployment impact

This branch changes build configuration and its operator guide only. Release preparation included read-only Kubernetes workload and Helm-value inspection, EN service/image inspection, read-only PostgreSQL migration and identity queries, Bitcoin RPC chain queries, and main-node API queries. Exact named database secret keys were read locally for target comparison; no values were published. No deployment, service, schema, database row, or secret value was changed. No temporary pod, restart, migration, or wallet write was performed. Merging permits build-only CI on `main`; it does not publish release images or deploy services. controller: #8950
BDD/spec contract: #11178
Integration/source authority: #10651
Candidate profiles: #11170 / #11172
Generic provider expectation authority: #7109 and current provider-owned fixtures
Position/raw-byte authorities: #2298 / #7713
Deterministic client simulation consumer: #11103
Actual-host adapter/consumers: #10673 / #10676 / #10679 / #10681 / #10684 / #10691 / #10693
Platform/public consumers: #10733 / #9010 / #9012
Support importer: #7122 / #9016

## State

**Blocked until #11178 supplies stable Lite XL BDD scenario IDs.**

Fixture mechanics and independent semantic expectations can be researched beforehand, but final manifest cells must map to accepted scenario IDs rather than inventing a second product specification.

## One-PR result

Create one versioned, machine-readable **Lite XL semantic workspace and expectation manifest** shared by deterministic client simulation, exact-process/profile proof, real-host semantic lanes, platform rows, managed-package proof, and released/public replay.

This is the executable expectation authority. It does not launch Lite XL, implement the client or server, compose patches, derive expected values from `perllsp`, or award support.

## Why this is separate

Keep these objects distinct:

```text
#11178 BDD/spec ledger
  user-visible journey and profile/evidence meaning

this manifest
  exact source/config/wire bytes, anchors, expected facts and wrong-subject controls

#11103 client simulation
  deterministic client mechanics against exact staged source

#10673/#9008 actual-host receipts
  what exact Lite XL/client/profile/server/platform subjects actually did
```

A fixture is not the product specification. A static expectation is not a host observation. A real host must not choose convenient expected values after seeing the result.

## Manifest contract

Define a versioned schema equivalent to `lite_xl_fixture_expectations.v1`.

Each fixture/cell records at least:

```text
stable fixture/scenario/cell IDs
owning #11178 BDD scenario ID
claim profile and evidence ceiling
source/config/process/UI role
role-relative path or virtual subject
exact bytes or governed fixture reference
SHA-256 and newline/BOM/encoding disposition
content-derived anchors and occurrence rules
expected semantic payload/result fingerprint
explicit false-subject facts
ordered actions/mutations/barriers
expected provider/document/root/version transition
required client-visible application/effect
simulation/exact-process/host/platform/public consumers
supported/conditional/unsupported/not_proven disposition
privacy/redaction class
```

A cell may project a governed provider/parser/position expectation rather than copy it. The reference and transformation are load-bearing.

## Canonical umbrella workspace

Use one small coherent umbrella fixture containing:

```text
umbrella/
  parent-or-sibling-distractor/
  intended-perl-project/
    .perl-lsp.toml
    safe Lite XL project data where admitted
    malicious .lite_lsp.lua sentinel
    lib/
    t/
    bin-or-script roles
    formatting/edit roles
    large-wire roles
  second-perl-project/
```

The intended root, sibling distractor and second root must contain equivalent names with deliberately different values/docs/content so wrong root/provider answers fail semantically.

### Activation roles

Provide independent files for:

```text
.pl .PL .pm .t .psgi .cgi .fcgi
```

and explicit negative/deferred roles for:

```text
.pod .ep .tt .tt2 .mason .xs
extensionless shebang
untitled before first save
Raku/NQP/P6-family distractors where useful
```

Activation expectations require actual exact-provider attach/open at host stages; syntax detection alone is insufficient.

## Configuration and trust expectations

Include independently reviewable inputs for:

- safe user-owned Lite XL settings;
- safe project data configuration after #10653;
- malicious project `.lite_lsp.lua` that writes a canary/sentinel if executed;
- `.perl-lsp.toml` setting with an externally observable semantic effect;
- explicit `false`, `true`, `0`, empty string, JSON null, empty array, empty object and nested values;
- ordered duplicate `workspace/configuration` items;
- inherited array followed by shorter and empty-array overrides;
- same workspace with two server-definition settings subjects for cache-isolation proof;
- malformed project data and out-of-root `scopeUri` controls.

Expected responses must preserve exact JSON shape/cardinality/order and demonstrate behavior, not merely trace presence.

## Diagnostic expectations

Define a deterministic target diagnostic with:

```text
stable code/source/message class
exact source role + content-derived range anchor
initial malformed bytes
second distinct malformed bytes
repaired bytes
unrelated legitimate diagnostic distractor where useful
versioned publication sequence
stale older nonempty publication
stale older empty publication
old server/provider generation publication
```

Required oracles:

- exact target appears at the expected live-document position;
- newer malformed state replaces the target for the current version;
- repair removes/replaces the target through a current publication;
- unrelated diagnostics/count changes cannot satisfy the cell;
- stale empty/nonempty/provider-generation publications cannot alter current state;
- non-BMP text before the diagnostic catches raw UTF-16-as-byte-column errors.

Do not make total diagnostic count the oracle.

## Completion, hover, signature and navigation

### Completion

Provide:

- content-derived trigger position;
- exact expected item identity/label/detail/kind at the strength owned by provider authority;
- same-prefix distractor items;
- ordinary and snippet/non-snippet disposition;
- resolve/additionalTextEdit auto-import case;
- exact final buffer bytes, selection/cursor disposition and unrelated sentinels;
- stale response after an intervening same-caret edit.

### Hover/signature

- exact target symbol and semantically discriminating content/active-parameter facts;
- same-name wrong symbol/root/provider controls;
- nonblank-but-wrong and stale prior-generation controls.

### Navigation/references/symbols

- exact target role, URI/path identity, content digest and range anchor;
- same-name parent/sibling target with different content;
- Location and LocationLink roles where provider output supports them;
- blank target line followed by prettier preview text so preview mutation fails;
- open dirty target whose live bytes differ from disk;
- multiple references and selected-result navigation;
- document/workspace symbol identities and stale root/query controls.

## Editing expectations

Use one coherent edit workspace with exact pre/post bytes.

### Same-document transaction

Include deliberately:

- unsorted edits;
- edits before/after one another;
- zero-length insert + replacement;
- overlapping/invalid/out-of-bounds controls;
- CRLF and non-BMP ranges;
- ordinary completion plus additional import edit;
- formatting edits whose returned order is shuffled;
- unrelated sentinels;
- expected dirty state and selection transform.

### Multi-file rename

Include:

- exact symbol roles across multiple files;
- active dirty target and closed target;
- expected final bytes for every admitted target;
- unsupported `documentChanges`/resource-operation control;
- missing/invalid target control;
- post-rename definition/reference expectation under the new name;
- old-name negative result.

Returned edit objects are not success.

## Document/version/lifecycle expectations

Define ordered actions without scheduler sleeps for:

```text
open → edit → edit
edit → save → edit
edit → undo → redo
close → reopen same URI/same bytes
first save untitled/unsupported → supported Perl filename
Save As supported → supported same root
Save As supported → unsupported
Save As across selected roots
explicit restart with held old response/diagnostic/timer
close last matching document and reopen
forced harness assertion after child start
normal editor close
```

Expected facts include exact server/document-session identities, monotonic version sequence within a session, one didClose/didOpen transition, once-only document replay, stale old-generation rejection and zero final process/timer/watcher ownership.

## Position, path and wire fixtures

Reference #2298/#7713 where possible and add host/client roles for:

### Position/newline

```text
non-BMP before diagnostic/navigation/edit
multi-byte BMP before position
CRLF and LF roles
multiline/zero-length ranges
actual selected text-sync branch and observed payload
```

### URI/path

```text
POSIX path with spaces, #, ?, %, quotes, Unicode and emoji
Windows drive path
admitted UNC or explicit unsupported disposition
file://localhost and remote-authority controls
malformed percent escape
encoded NUL/control
non-file URI
```

### Large/outbound wire

Create a deterministic document over the Lite XL large-message threshold with:

```text
quotes/backslashes
all JSON control characters where source/fixture representation permits
CRLF
non-BMP/multi-byte UTF-8 across chunk boundaries
sentinels exactly before/at/after chunk boundaries
```

Retain exact decoded text bytes and expected provider/diagnostic discriminator after edit.

### Inbound framing

Provide frame byte fixtures for:

```text
split headers/bodies
multiple frames + remainder
missing/malformed/duplicate/overflow Content-Length
oversized declared body
truncated header/body
valid large response near admitted bound
```

These are client protocol fixtures, not provider semantic expectations.

## Root and watcher expectations

The umbrella fixture must prove:

```text
nearest intended Perl root wins over umbrella/.git distractor
.perl-lsp.toml from selected root changes behavior
sibling project facts cannot satisfy workspace results
closed dependency change updates current answer
external .cgi or .fcgi create becomes visible
external change is reflected
external delete removes exact fact
watcher/root/server generation cleanup after restart/close
```

A hidden restart/reopen cannot satisfy live watcher currentness. Multiple roots remain explicitly unsupported/not-proven unless #10767 admits them.

## Provider and wrong-subject controls

Every core semantic workspace must contain false-green controls for:

```text
PerlNavigator/another Perl provider
ambient wrong perllsp binary
same-name package/symbol in wrong root
same version text with different binary bytes
stale composed profile/tree digest
old server/document generation
previous source bytes
server logs without client consumption
capability bit/command visibility without behavior
```

The manifest records the exact subject that must win and the subjects that must not satisfy the cell.

## Stage reuse

The same core fixture/expectation IDs must be usable by:

```text
#11103 simulation
#8960 exact-process/profile
#10676 Linux baseline host
#10679/#10681/#10684/#10691/#10693 semantic lanes
#10733 native Windows/macOS bounded rows
#9010 staged managed package
#9012 released/public replay
```

Subject identity changes by stage; semantic expectations do not silently weaken. Platform-specific path/process/watcher roles are additive and exact.

## Mapping and generation

Generate/check:

```text
BDD scenario ID
→ fixture/expectation cell
→ #11103 deterministic test ID where applicable
→ exact-process/protocol receipt cell where applicable
→ actual-host observation cell
→ support-registry cell
```

Every required #9008 core cell has one expectation owner or explicit unsupported/not_proven disposition.

Generation/validation must be deterministic and second-run clean. Exact byte-sensitive files follow repository raw-byte/checkout policy. Human-readable projections are not byte authority.

## Independent oracle rule

Expected semantic outputs must be:

- static and independently reviewed;
- imported from a governed provider/parser/position authority; or
- derived by a separate simple reference transformation whose independence is explicit.

Never capture/bless the expected result from the same `perllsp` provider path or client candidate under test.

## Required negative controls

Fail when:

1. expected values are generated/blessed from the production provider/client under test;
2. wrong parent/sibling/provider/binary can satisfy a core cell;
3. any diagnostic/count/nonempty result satisfies an exact target;
4. completion/hover/navigation checks lack semantic target/application facts;
5. configuration trace passes without expected behavior/value shape;
6. formatting/rename returns but final bytes/selection/currentness are absent;
7. previous-generation result satisfies post-edit/restart expectation;
8. host stage chooses a different convenient fixture/expected value;
9. hand-maintained line number survives where a content-derived anchor is required;
10. byte-sensitive fixture is normalized by checkout/generation;
11. >50 KiB cell drops below the threshold;
12. live watcher cell uses restart/reopen;
13. one platform/profile/install stage weakens core semantics silently;
14. raw private paths, canary secrets or unbounded source/logs enter public projections;
15. BDD scenario has no fixture/simulation/host/support disposition.

## Implementation order

1. Consume accepted #11178 scenario IDs and current generic provider/position/text-sync authorities.
2. Inventory useful existing Perl semantic fixtures; reference rather than duplicate when they already own the oracle.
3. Write wrong-root/provider/binary, weak-diagnostic/completion/hover/navigation, trace-only-config, unapplied-edit, stale-generation, small-file, hidden-restart and raw-log falsifiers.
4. Define the schema/validator and stable cell IDs.
5. Build the umbrella semantic workspace and exact configuration/diagnostic/provider/edit expectations.
6. Add protocol/path/wire/lifecycle/watcher roles and governed references.
7. Generate the full scenario→fixture→simulation→host→support map.
8. Run schema, raw-byte, anchor uniqueness, deterministic generation and second-run checks.

## Review map

PR body must include:

```text
BDD scenarios consumed
new/reused fixture IDs
independent expectation sources
wrong-subject and weak-oracle controls
byte/anchor integrity
configuration/security canaries
currentness/version/lifecycle actions
position/path/wire roles
host/platform/public reuse map
generated outputs and checks
what no client/server/host/support behavior is changed
```

## Acceptance

- [ ] One canonical Lite XL fixture/expectation manifest serves simulation, exact-process, actual-host, platform, managed and public stages.
- [ ] Core diagnostic/completion/hover/navigation/settings/edit facts are semantically discriminating and application-aware.
- [ ] Root/provider/binary/currentness false subjects are load-bearing negatives.
- [ ] JSON/configuration, document/version, diagnostic, path/position, wire, watcher and lifecycle expectations are exact and independently owned.
- [ ] Content-derived anchors replace fragile line-number/count assertions.
- [ ] Stage/platform/profile rows reuse core semantics without cross-subject inference or silent weakening.
- [ ] BDD, simulation, receipt and support mappings are complete and deterministic.
- [ ] No server/client output is used as its own expected oracle.
- [ ] No Lite XL process, client/server implementation, candidate composition, support promotion, package publication or external action occurs.

## Codex execution contract

**Suggested branch:** `codex/lite-xl-fixture-expectations`

Start after #11178 scenario IDs are current. Reuse current provider/parser/position fixture authorities and mine existing editor fixtures for mechanics only; do not retain weak count/nonempty/log assertions as authority. Write wrong-subject/weak-oracle/security/currentness/unapplied-edit/small-file/hidden-restart falsifiers first. Implement the manifest, umbrella workspace, governed projections and mappings. Stop before #11103 client-product changes or #10673 actual-host work.

## Non-goals

LLM 에이전트(와 사람)가 **번호로 선을 살리고·지우고·점을 편집**할 수 있습니다. 편집은 먼저 제안(빨강 = 사라짐, 초록 = 생김)으로 보이고, 확인한 뒤 적용합니다. 이전에 커밋하지 않았던 작업도 이 브랜치의 첫 커밋(`e3ef4cf`)에 들어 있습니다. - LLM 에이전트 사이드 패널 (OpenRouter / Claude Code / Codex, MCP) - Claude Code 로그인 확인과 로그인 창 열기 - GUI에서 RViz 3D 재생 열기 - 입력 이미지를 컬러 원본으로 표시 ## 주요 변경 - **`stages.py`:** 단계 7개(원본·전처리·선 검출·뼈대·겹침 제거·이어 붙이기·단순화)와 해시 캐시 `Pipeline`을 추가했습니다. 바뀐 단계부터만 다시 계산합니다. 기존 `run_pipeline()`은 이 파이프라인을 부르며, **리팩터링 전 결과와 완전히 같습니다**(합성 16건, 샘플 12건 기준값 비교). - **색 차이(Lab) 선 검출:** 밝기가 비슷한 색의 경계도 잡습니다. 파이프라인이 버린 조각은 이유(small / spur / overlap)와 함께 "살릴 후보"로 기록합니다. - **`edits.py`:** 점 편집(옮기기·지우기·넣기·매끄럽게·자르기·잇기), 모양 기반 재적용, 초록/빨강 그림을 담당합니다. - **`session.py`:** - 번호표, 제안 → 적용(exclude/only, 잇기·자르기 묶음) → 되돌리기 흐름을 관리합니다. - 편집은 모양으로 기록해 다시 계산해도 유지됩니다. - 다시 계산이나 적용이 실패하면 이전 상태로 되돌립니다. - 종이 배치(mm)를 고정해, 편집해도 좌표가 움직이지 않습니다. - **GUI:** - 단계 띠(썸네일), 큰 보기(휠 확대·끌어 이동·원본 겹치기), 단계별 조절 칸(자동 생성)을 넣었습니다. - 값을 바꾸면 0.3초 뒤 자동으로 다시 계산합니다. - 편집 단계에는 번호 딱지, 버린 선, 제안 바가 있습니다. - **에이전트 도구:** `set_params` 스키마를 단계 정의에서 만들고, `view`로 단계별 결과를 볼 수 있습니다. - 새 도구: `list_strokes`, `get_stroke`, `propose_edits`(10종), `apply_proposals`, `discard_proposals` - 기존 `delete_strokes`/`delete_region`은 `propose_edits`로 합쳤습니다. ## 확인 - `python -m unittest discover -s tests`: **134개 통과**, pyflakes 깨끗 - 새 테스트 파일: `test_stages`, `test_edits`, `test_golden`, `test_gui_smoke` - `test_agent`에 추가: `EditSessionTest`, `ReviewFixesTest`, `MinorFixesTest` - **속도:** 샘플 6장 전체 계산 0.55~1.65초(첫 실행은 skimage 로딩으로 약 3초), 뒤 단계만 바꾸면 0.003~0.011초 - **화면 확인:** 라이트/다크 모드에서 단계 보기와 편집 단계(제안 4건, 딱지 빼기, 확대 시 번호)를 캡처해 직접 확인했습니다. - **코드 리뷰:** 새 리뷰어가 브랜치 전체를 검토했습니다.
